# Discovering Regulatory Relationships Across 3D Genome Architecture and DNA Methylation: Context-Adjusted Reliability-Aware Enhancer–Gene Inference (CARA-E2G)

## 1. Executive Research Summary and Epistemological Framework

Identifying which distal noncoding cis-regulatory elements (enhancers) functionally regulate which target genes across the human genome remains a foundational challenge in regulatory genomics and complex trait genetics ([Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/); [Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/)). While biochemical assays profile millions of open chromatin regions, histone modifications, three-dimensional (3D) chromatin loops, and base-resolution CpG methylation states across hundreds of biosamples, physical proximity or biochemical activity at a distal locus does not guarantee a causal transcriptional effect on a nearby gene ([Gasperini et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690346/); [Hoellinger et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9999192/)). High-throughput genetic perturbation screens using clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi), such as CRISPRi-FlowFISH ([Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/); [Nasser et al., 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9153265/)), Perturb-seq ([Gasperini et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690346/)), and targeted Perturb-seq (TAP-seq; [Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/)), provide direct functional ground truth by quantifying target mRNA reduction upon KRAB-dCas9 repression of candidate enhancers.

This study investigates a specific methodological question: **Does integrating base-resolution DNA methylation patterns (from Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing, WGBS) and 3D chromatin contacts (from intact/in situ Hi-C) with 1D chromatin activity and gene expression provide reproducible, complementary predictive information for identifying functional enhancer–gene (E–G) relationships in held-out genomic regions?**

To maintain epistemological rigor, the analysis explicitly separates three distinct scientific claims that are frequently conflated in multi-omics literature:

1. **Claim 1 (Predictive Gain from Multi-Omics Integration)**: Combining compatible features from WGBS DNA methylation, 3D chromatin conformation, and 1D regulatory activity improves out-of-sample precision and recall on held-out chromosomes relative to established methods (`Activity-by-Contact` and `ENCODE-rE2G-Core`).
2. **Claim 2 (Complementary Information Content)**: DNA methylation and 3D chromatin contacts contribute statistically independent predictive signals that are not redundant with linear genomic distance ($d_{EG}$) or 1D open chromatin/acetylation (`DNase-seq` and `H3K27ac`).
3. **Claim 3 (Genuine Biological Regulation vs. Confounding Artifacts)**: The inferred associations reflect genuine cis-regulatory enhancer activity rather than passive background correlation, megabase-scale cancer replication-timing artifacts, or locus-level training-test data leakage.

Empirical evaluation on $N = 10,375$ power-filtered ($\ge 80\%$ power) candidate E–G pairs ($472$ functional positives, $9,903$ negatives across $618$ target gene loci on $23$ chromosomes in human K562 erythroleukemia cells, `ENCSR998YDI`) demonstrates that **naive integration of focal DNA methylation fails** ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0044$, $p = 0.302$). Diagnostic auditing reveals why: $37.89\%$ of candidate E–G pairs in K562 reside within megabase-scale **Partially Methylated Domains (PMDs)**—late-replicating, heterochromatic B-compartment regions exhibiting disordered intermediate-to-low background methylation ([Burger et al., 2013](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3763559/); [Fortin & Hansen, 2015](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4574526/)). Treating raw focal unmethylation ($1 - M_{\text{focal}}$) as an active enhancer signal conflates passive PMD hypomethylation with transcription-factor-driven focal demethylation, causing $58.0\%$ of top false positives to cluster inside PMDs.

By formulating **CARA-E2G** (*Context-Adjusted Reliability-Aware Enhancer-to-Gene* inference)—which decouples focal pioneer-factor demethylation from regional 50-kb PMD background methylation, discounts noisy low-coverage or CpG-poor elements via binomial reliability weights, and shrinks sparse long-range Hi-C contacts toward a fractal-globule power-law prior—held-out chromosome AUPRC increases from $0.5950$ (`ENCODE-rE2G-Core`) and $0.4606$ (`ABC`) to **$0.6858$** ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0908$, $95\%$ locus-clustered bootstrap CI $[+0.0681, +0.1142]$, $p = 0.0020$), while Precision at $70\%$ Recall rises from $0.4148$ to **$0.5304$** ($+11.56$ percentage points) and PMD false-positive contamination drops from $58.0\%$ to $21.0\%$.

## 2. Focused Literature Review and Competing Methods Analysis

### 2.1 Evolution of Enhancer–Gene Linking Paradigms

Computational approaches for linking distal regulatory elements to target genes have evolved across four methodological generations ([Hoellinger et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9999192/); [Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/)):

1. **Genomic Distance and Unsupervised Cross-Cell-Type Correlation**: Early studies assigned candidate enhancers (defined by DNase I hypersensitive sites, DHSs, or ENCODE candidate cis-regulatory elements, cCREs) to the nearest expressed transcription start site (TSS) or correlated enhancer accessibility with promoter expression across panels of cell types ([Sheffield et al., 2013](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9999192/); `EpiMap` by Boix et al., 2021). However, CRISPRi tiling screens demonstrated that enhancers frequently skip proximal genes to regulate distal targets and that cross-cell-type correlations suffer from low precision ($<25\%$ at $70\%$ recall) when distinguishing co-regulated bystanders from causal cis-enhancers ([Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/)).
2. **Loop-Calling and Supervised Physical Interaction Classifiers**: Methods such as `TargetFinder` ([Whalen et al., 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9999192/)) framed E–G linking as predicting binary 3D chromatin loops derived from Hi-C, Promoter Capture Hi-C (PCHi-C), or ChIA-PET using gradient boosting over 1D epigenomic marks (including DNA methylation and histone modifications in the enhancer–promoter window). Subsequent audits revealed two severe flaws in this paradigm: first, random pair-level cross-validation leaked shared genomic windows between training and test sets; second, models trained on physical loop calls failed to generalize to functional CRISPRi perturbation benchmarks ($\text{AUPRC} < 0.25$ on K562 CRISPRi-FlowFISH; [Hoellinger et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9999192/)).
3. **Biochemical Activity-by-Contact (ABC) Mechanistic Modeling**: [Fulco et al. (2019)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/) and [Nasser et al. (2021)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9153265/) introduced the unsupervised **Activity-by-Contact (ABC)** model, positing that an enhancer's quantitative regulatory contribution to gene $G$ is proportional to its local biochemical activity ($A_E = \sqrt{\text{DNase}_E \cdot \text{H3K27ac}_E}$) multiplied by its 3D contact frequency with the promoter ($C_{EG}$, measured by 5-kb Knight–Ruiz normalized Hi-C or approximated by a fractal-globule power-law $d_{EG}^{-0.87}$), normalized across all candidate elements within $5\text{ Mb}$ of $G$. While ABC substantially outperformed distance and loop-calling baselines, it assumes strictly additive enhancer action, treats all target promoters as equally responsive, and is vulnerable to multiplicative variance inflation when $C_{EG}$ is estimated from sparse Hi-C bin counts at distances $>100\text{ kb}$.
4. **Supervised Perturbation-Trained Classifiers and Multimodal Deep Architectures**:
   - **ENCODE-rE2G** ([Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/)) trained L2-regularized logistic regression classifiers directly on $10,411$ harmonized K562 CRISPRi element–gene pairs (`ENCSR998YDI`) using leave-one-chromosome-out (LOCO) validation. `ENCODE-rE2G` (13 features from DNase-seq and average Hi-C) and `ENCODE-rE2G-Extended` (47 features adding H3K27ac, cell-type-specific intact Hi-C, ChIA-PET, and external model scores) demonstrated that two biological modifiers tune ABC: (i) **ubiquitously expressed housekeeping promoters** are $\sim 5$-fold less sensitive to distal enhancers, and (ii) **local enhancer synergy** (the count and summed activity of neighboring enhancers within $5\text{ kb}$) super-additively boosts regulatory efficacy. Notably, neither `ENCODE-rE2G` nor `ENCODE-rE2G-Extended` incorporated base-resolution DNA methylation.
   - **scE2G** ([Sheth et al., 2024](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.11.23.624931v1.full-text)) extended the supervised rE2G framework to single-cell ATAC-seq and 10x Multiome (scATAC + scRNA-seq) data by combining pseudobulk ABC scores, promoter ubiquity class, and single-cell Kendall $\tau$ rank correlation between chromatin accessibility and gene expression within a cell type, capturing stochastic transcriptional bursting at loci such as `TFRC`.
   - **GraphReg / Seq-GraphReg** ([Karbalayghareh et al., 2022](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9104700/)) used Graph Attention Networks (GATs) over 3D interaction graphs (HiChIP/Hi-C edges) to predict CAGE-seq expression and prioritize enhancers via feature attribution across $1\text{--}2\text{ Mb}$.
   - **EPInformer** ([Lin et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11312614/)) introduced a scalable transformer framework integrating promoter sequence ($2\text{ kb}$) and up to $60$ ABC-nominated enhancer sequences ($256\text{ bp}$) with DNase-seq, H3K27ac, and Hi-C contact features (`EPInformer-PE-Activity-HiC`), evaluated under 12-fold cross-chromosome validation on K562 and GM12878 CAGE/RNA-seq expression and CRISPRi enhancer prioritization via attention weights.
   - **DNALONGBENCH** ([Cheng et al., 2025](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39829833/)) established a standardized long-range DNA sequence benchmark (spanning up to $1\text{ Mb}$) across five tasks—including K562 CRISPRi enhancer–target gene interaction (derived from Gasperini et al., 2019), eQTLs, and 3D contact maps—demonstrating that long-range sequence foundation models (`HyenaDNA`, `Caduceus-Ph`, `Caduceus-PS`, `Enformer`) struggle to match epigenome-informed models on distal enhancer linking ($>100\text{ kb}$) without explicit 3D chromatin and local epigenetic state inputs.

### 2.2 DNA Methylation at Enhancers: Focal Pioneer-Factor Demethylation vs. Cancer PMDs

Seminal methylome studies by [Stadler et al. (2011)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3160184/) and [Burger et al. (2013)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3763559/) (`MethylSeekR`) established that active mammalian regulatory regions partition into two distinct classes in Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (WGBS) profiles:
- **Unmethylated Regions (UMRs)**: CpG-rich ($\ge 30$ CpGs), completely unmethylated ($<10\%$ methylation) regions that predominantly mark proximal CpG-island (CGI) promoters and remain constitutively unmethylated across tissues regardless of gene expression level.
- **Low-Methylated Regions (LMRs)**: CpG-poor ($3\text{--}29$ CpGs), distal intergenic or intronic regions exhibiting locally reduced methylation ($10\%\text{--}50\%$) relative to a fully methylated ($\sim 80\%$) genomic background. LMRs are dynamically created when lineage-specific pioneer transcription factors (such as GATA1, GATA2, TAL1, SPI1/PU.1, and KLF1 in erythroid/hematopoietic cells) bind nucleosomal DNA and recruit TET dioxygenases, actively demethylating consecutive CpGs around the TF binding footprint ([Burger et al., 2013](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3763559/); [Lea et al., 2018](https://elifesciences.org/articles/37513)).

Furthermore, high-throughput methylation-sensitive reporter screening (**mSTARR-seq** in K562; [Lea et al., 2018](https://elifesciences.org/articles/37513)) proved that CpG methylation causally silences a specific subset of methylation-dependent (MD) enhancers by sterically hindering methyl-sensitive TF binding or recruiting methyl-CpG-binding domain (MBD) repressors, and confirmed that GATA-family TFs drive active post-transfection demethylation ($6.7$-fold enrichment, $p = 3.6 \times 10^{-4}$).

However, in immortalized cell lines and cancer genomes—including **K562** (`ENCSR765JPC`)—the canonical high-methylation background ($\sim 80\%$) is disrupted across $30\%\text{--}40\%$ of the genome by **Partially Methylated Domains (PMDs)** ([Burger et al., 2013](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3763559/); [Fortin & Hansen, 2015](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4574526/)). PMDs are megabase-scale domains (mean length $\sim 153\text{ kb}$) that coincide with late-replicating, nuclear-lamina-associated, heterochromatic Hi-C B compartments where maintenance DNA methyltransferase (DNMT1) fails to keep pace with rapid mitotic division. Within PMDs, non-regulatory DNA passively drifts to intermediate or low methylation ($25\%\text{--}50\%$) with high site-to-site variance. As [Burger et al. (2013)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3763559/) warned, failing to decouple PMDs causes thousands of passive hypomethylated windows inside transcriptionally repressed chromatin to be falsely classified as active LMR enhancers.

## 3. Selection and Verification of the Biological System (Human K562, GRCh38)

### 3.1 Rationale for Selecting Homo sapiens K562

A rigorous investigation of whether DNA methylation and 3D chromatin contacts improve functional enhancer–gene inference requires a biological system where **all four data pillars**—(1) large-scale functional CRISPR enhancer perturbations, (2) high-resolution 3D chromatin interaction maps, (3) base-resolution whole-genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS), and (4) 1D chromatin accessibility, histone acetylation, and gene expression—are measured in the **exact same biological state**. Mixing methylation from one tissue with Hi-C or CRISPR perturbations from another introduces severe cell-identity confounding.

Across all public repositories (ENCODE, Roadmap Epigenomics, 4D Nucleome, IHEC, and plant/model organism databases), the human **K562** chronic myelogenous leukemia (erythroleukemia lineage) Tier 1 ENCODE cell line is the **only biological system** possessing >10,000 power-filtered CRISPRi enhancer–gene perturbation measurements matched with deep intact Hi-C, WGBS, DNase-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq, polyA+ RNA-seq, and mSTARR-seq methylation-perturbation data on assembly **GRCh38 (hg38)**. Moreover, because K562 exhibits both classic lineage-specific pioneer-factor LMRs (driven by GATA1/GATA2/TAL1/KLF1) and extensive cancer-associated Partially Methylated Domains (PMDs covering $37.89\%$ of tested E–G pairs), it provides an ideal proving ground to test whether context-adjusted methylation modeling can separate causal enhancer demethylation from domain-scale replication-timing artifacts.

### 3.2 Verified Data Provenance, Accessions, and Feature Definitions

All datasets are aligned to human reference genome **GRCh38 / hg38** under open Creative Commons / unrestricted ENCODE data release licenses:

1. **CRISPRi Functional Enhancer–Gene Benchmark (`ENCSR998YDI`)**: Harmonized by the ENCODE4 Distal Regulation Working Group ([Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/); `EPCrisprBenchmark_ensemble_data_GRCh38.tsv.gz` in [EngreitzLab/CRISPR_comparison](https://github.com/EngreitzLab/CRISPR_comparison)). Integrates power-filtered ($\ge 80\%$ statistical power to detect a $25\%$ effect size) candidate E–G pairs from four K562 CRISPRi studies:
   - **CRISPRi-FlowFISH tiling screens** ([Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/); [Nasser et al., 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9153265/)): $5,315$ pairs ($162$ positives, $3.05\%$ positive rate), exhaustively tiling all DHS elements within $450\text{ kb}\text{--}2\text{ Mb}$ of $30+$ genes (`MYC`, `GATA1`, `HDAC6`, `HBG1`, `HBG2`, `HBE1`, `PIM1`, `PRKAR2B`, `TFRC`, `BCL11A`, `KLF1`, `JUNB`, `PRDX2`, `NFE2`, `TAL1`, `LMO2`, `SPI1`, `FECH`, etc.).
   - **Multiplex single-cell Perturb-seq / crisprQTL** ([Gasperini et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690346/), `GEO:GSE120861`): $3,857$ power-filtered pairs ($243$ positives, $6.30\%$ positive rate), including monoclonal deletion-validated loci (`NMU`, `CITED2`, `GLUL`) and singleton-replicated loci (`PRKCB`, `PTGER3`, `GYPC`).
   - **Targeted Perturb-seq (TAP-seq)** ([Schraivogel et al., 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/)): $1,203$ power-filtered pairs ($67$ positives, $5.57\%$ positive rate) on chromosomes 8 and 11.
   - **Total Harmonized Dataset**: $N = 10,375$ candidate pairs ($472$ positives $[4.55\%]$, $9,903$ negatives $[95.45\%]$) across $618$ target gene loci on all $23$ chromosomes (`chr1`–`chr22`, `chrX`), restricted to distal elements with TSS distance $d_{EG} \in [500\text{ bp}, 2.5\text{ Mb}]$ (median $d_{EG} = 66,503\text{ bp}$ across all pairs; median $d_{EG} = 10,353.5\text{ bp}$ across validated positives).
2. **1D Chromatin Accessibility (`ENCSR000EOT`, file `ENCFF257HEE`)**: K562 DNase-seq read density (RPM) quantified across $500\text{ bp}$ centered on each candidate element ($\text{DNase}_E$) and $\pm 500\text{ bp}$ around the target gene TSS ($\text{DNase}_P$).
3. **1D Histone H3K27 Acetylation (`ENCSR000AKP`, file `ENCFF232RQF`)**: K562 H3K27ac ChIP-seq RPM quantified across $\pm 500\text{ bp}$ around each candidate element ($\text{H3K27ac}_E$). Intrinsic biochemical activity is $A_E = \sqrt{\text{DNase}_E \cdot \text{H3K27ac}_E}$, accompanied by $5\text{ kb}$ local enhancer synergy features ($N_{5\text{kb}}(E)$ and $\sum_{E' \in 5\text{kb}} A_{E'}$).
4. **3D Chromatin Conformation (`ENCSR479XDG`, file `ENCFF621AIY` & `ENCSR382HAW`, file `ENCFF134PUN`)**: K562 intact/in situ Hi-C contact frequency at $5\text{ kb}$ bin resolution with Knight–Ruiz (KR) matrix balancing ($C_{EG}^{\text{KR}}$), paired with raw contact read depth $n_{\text{reads}}(E,G)$ and 35-biosample average Hi-C contact.
5. **Whole-Genome Bisulfite Sequencing (`ENCSR765JPC`, files `ENCFF721JMB`, `ENCFF867JRG`; `GEO:GSE86747`)**: Base-resolution CpG methylation calls in K562 processed to extract four regional features per candidate element $E$:
   - Focal element CpG methylation fraction $M_{\text{focal}}(E) \in [0, 1]$ within the $500\text{ bp}$ DHS window.
   - Regional background CpG methylation fraction $M_{\text{bg},50\text{kb}}(E) \in [0, 1]$ across the flanking $\pm 25\text{ kb}$ domain (excluding $\pm 2\text{ kb}$ around annotated CGIs/DHSs), which cleanly separates **Highly Methylated Domains (HMDs, mean $M_{\text{bg}} = 0.81$)** from **Partially Methylated Domains (PMDs, mean $M_{\text{bg}} = 0.35$)**.
   - Local CpG dinucleotide count $k_E$ within the $500\text{ bp}$ element and mean WGBS read coverage $n_{\text{cov}}(E)$.
6. **Gene Expression & Promoter Class (`ENCSR000AEM`, `GEO:GSE78557`)**: K562 polyA+ RNA-seq expression ($\text{TPM}_G$) and binary promoter ubiquity indicator $I_{\text{ubiq}}(G) \in \{0, 1\}$ denoting housekeeping genes uniformly expressed across ENCODE biosamples ($30.69\%$ of tested pairs).
7. **Functional Methylation-Sensitivity Assay (`eLife:37513`, [Lea et al., 2018](https://elifesciences.org/articles/37513))**: K562 mSTARR-seq $\log_2\text{FC}$ comparing unmethylated versus *M.SssI* enzymatically methylated reporter activity, annotating methylation-dependent (MD) regulatory loci ($\log_2\text{FC} > 0.85$).

## 4. Mathematical Formulation of Staged Baselines and Proposed Algorithm (CARA-E2G)

### 4.1 Staged Baselines (A through D)

To ensure fair, transparent benchmarking where every model is evaluated on identical candidate pairs and identical chromosome-holdout splits without privileged label access, we implement six staged baselines:

- **Baseline A — Genomic Proximity**: Ranks candidate E–G pairs strictly by inverse genomic distance to the target gene TSS:
  $$S_{\text{Prox}}(E, G) = \frac{1}{d_{EG}}, \quad d_{EG} = |x_E - x_{\text{TSS}(G)}|$$
- **Baseline B — 3D Chromatin Contact**: Ranks candidate E–G pairs by 5-kb Knight–Ruiz normalized K562 Hi-C contact frequency:
  $$S_{\text{Contact}}(E, G) = C_{EG}^{\text{KR}}$$
- **Baseline C1 — Naive Methylation + Activity (Unadjusted for PMDs)**: Tests the standard assumption that low focal CpG methylation ($1 - M_{\text{focal}}(E)$) combined with open/acetylated chromatin and distance decay predicts enhancer function:
  $$S_{\text{NaiveMeth}}(E, G) = \big(1 - M_{\text{focal}}(E)\big)\cdot \frac{\log(1 + A_E)}{\sqrt{d_{EG} / 1000}}$$
- **Baseline C2 — Context-Decoupled Methylation + Activity (PMD-Adjusted)**: Replaces raw focal unmethylation with positive focal demethylation relative to the flanking $50\text{ kb}$ domain background ($M_{\text{bg},50\text{kb}}(E) - M_{\text{focal}}(E)$):
  $$S_{\text{DecoupledMeth}}(E, G) = \Big(0.2 + \max\big(0, M_{\text{bg},50\text{kb}}(E) - M_{\text{focal}}(E)\big)\Big)\cdot \frac{\log(1 + A_E)}{\sqrt{d_{EG} / 1000}}$$
- **Baseline D1 — Activity-by-Contact (ABC Mechanistic Model; [Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/))**:
  $$\text{ABC}(E, G) = \frac{A_E \cdot C_{EG}^{\text{KR}}}{\sum_{E' \in \mathcal{N}_{5\text{Mb}}(G)} A_{E'} \cdot C_{E'G}^{\text{KR}}}$$
- **Baseline D2 — `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` (Supervised Logistic Classifier; [Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/))**: L2-regularized logistic regression trained via Leave-One-Chromosome-Out (LOCO) cross-validation over 10 core features capturing distance, enhancer DNase, enhancer H3K27ac, geometric activity $A_E$, promoter DNase, Hi-C contact $C_{EG}^{\text{KR}}$, $\log(1 + 100\cdot\text{ABC}_{EG})$, ubiquitous housekeeping promoter class $I_{\text{ubiq}}(G)$, and $5\text{ kb}$ neighboring enhancer count and summed activity.

### 4.2 Proposed Method: Context-Adjusted Reliability-Aware Enhancer–Gene Model (CARA-E2G)

Diagnostic inspection of the failure modes of `ABC`, `ENCODE-rE2G-Core`, and `Naive Methylation` reveals two fundamental statistical and biological flaws:
1. **PMD Confounding and Binomial Sampling Noise in WGBS**: In PMDs ($M_{\text{bg}} \approx 0.35$), passive loss of methylation makes $1 - M_{\text{focal}} \approx 0.65$ even at completely inactive intergenic sites. Moreover, when an element contains only $k_E \le 2$ CpGs or has low bisulfite read coverage $n_{\text{cov}}(E) < 5\times$, the sample fraction $M_{\text{focal}}(E)$ has high binomial variance $\text{Var}(\hat{M}) \approx M(1-M)/(n_{\text{cov}}\sqrt{k_E})$.
2. **Multiplicative Variance Inflation in Sparse Distal Hi-C Contacts**: At distances $d_{EG} > 50\text{ kb}$, 5-kb Hi-C bin pairs frequently contain only $1\text{--}5$ raw reads. Multiplying $A_E \cdot C_{EG}^{\text{KR}}$ directly in `ABC` amplifies Poisson shot noise.

**CARA-E2G** resolves both failure modes through three mathematical innovations:

#### Step 1: Reliability-Weighted PMD-Decoupled Methylation State
We define the **methylation measurement reliability weight** $r_m(E) \in [0, 1]$ as the product of a coverage saturation factor (with half-saturation constant $\tau_m = 15\times$) and a CpG footprint density factor (with characteristic scale $k_0 = 6$ CpGs, consistent with the 3–6 CpG minimum LMR footprint of [Burger et al., 2013](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3763559/)):
$$r_m(E) = \left(\frac{n_{\text{cov}}(E)}{n_{\text{cov}}(E) + \tau_m}\right) \cdot \left(1 - \exp\!\left(-\frac{k_E}{k_0}\right)\right)$$
We then decompose the focal methylation residual $\Delta M(E) = M_{\text{bg},50\text{kb}}(E) - M_{\text{focal}}(E)$ into two orthogonal, reliability-shrunk biological signals:
- **Active Focal TF Demethylation ($\Delta M_{\text{act}}$)**:
  $$\Delta M_{\text{act}}(E) = r_m(E) \cdot \max\!\big(0,\; M_{\text{bg},50\text{kb}}(E) - M_{\text{focal}}(E)\big)$$
- **Focal Hypermethylation Repression ($\Delta M_{\text{rep}}$)**:
  $$\Delta M_{\text{rep}}(E) = r_m(E) \cdot \max\!\big(0,\; M_{\text{focal}}(E) - M_{\text{bg},50\text{kb}}(E)\big)$$
And because active TF demethylation is particularly critical for confirming distal enhancers where 3D contact is weak, we include a smooth distance-gated interaction term:
$$\Phi_{\text{dist}\times\text{meth}}(E, G) = \Delta M_{\text{act}}(E) \cdot \sigma\!\Big(2.0\cdot \big(\log_{10} d_{EG} - 4.5\big)\Big)$$

#### Step 2: Empirical-Bayes Shrinkage of 3D Chromatin Contacts
Let $C_{\text{prior}}(d_{EG}) = \alpha_0 (d_{EG}/1000)^{-\gamma}$ ($\alpha_0 = 120, \gamma = 0.88$) denote the fractal-globule polymer expectation at distance $d_{EG}$, and let $r_c(E,G) = \frac{n_{\text{reads}}(E,G)}{n_{\text{reads}}(E,G) + \tau_c}$ ($\tau_c = 12$ reads) denote the Hi-C contact reliability weight. We compute the **empirical-Bayes shrunk contact estimate** $\hat{C}_{EG}$ in log-contact space:
$$\log \hat{C}_{EG} = r_c(E,G)\,\log C_{EG}^{\text{KR}} + \big(1 - r_c(E,G)\big)\,\log C_{\text{prior}}(d_{EG})$$
This yields both a denoised contact feature $\log(1 + \hat{C}_{EG})$, a shrunk loop-extrusion enrichment residual $L_{EG} = \log(\hat{C}_{EG} / C_{\text{prior}}(d_{EG}))$, and a **reliability-adjusted ABC score**:
$$\text{ABC}_{\text{CARA}}(E, G) = \frac{A_E \cdot \hat{C}_{EG} \cdot \exp\!\big(\eta_1 \Delta M_{\text{act}}(E) - \eta_2 \Delta M_{\text{rep}}(E)\big)}{\sum_{E' \in \mathcal{N}_{5\text{Mb}}(G)} A_{E'} \cdot \hat{C}_{E'G} \cdot \exp\!\big(\eta_1 \Delta M_{\text{act}}(E') - \eta_2 \Delta M_{\text{rep}}(E')\big)}$$

#### Step 3: Laplace-Calibrated Predictive Probability and Epistemic Uncertainty
Given the standardized 16-dimensional feature vector $\mathbf{x}_{EG} \in \mathbb{R}^{16}$, we fit an L2-regularized logistic regression parameter vector $\hat{\mathbf{w}}$ by minimizing the penalized negative log-likelihood on training chromosomes ($\lambda = 1.0$) and compute the inverse Hessian covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = (\mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{W} \mathbf{X} + \lambda \mathbf{I})^{-1}$. For any held-out test pair $(E,G)$, the marginal posterior predictive probability $\hat{P}(Y_{EG}=1 \mid \mathbf{x}_{EG})$ and epistemic uncertainty score $U(E,G) \in [0, 1]$ are:
$$\hat{P}(Y_{EG}=1 \mid \mathbf{x}_{EG}) = \sigma\!\left(\frac{\mathbf{x}_{EG}^\top \hat{\mathbf{w}}}{\sqrt{1 + \frac{\pi}{8}\,\mathbf{x}_{EG}^\top \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \mathbf{x}_{EG}}}\right), \quad U(E,G) = \frac{1}{2}\frac{\sqrt{\mathbf{x}_{EG}^\top \boldsymbol{\Sigma} \mathbf{x}_{EG}}}{\sigma_{\max}} + \frac{1}{2}\Big(1 - \frac{r_c(E,G) + r_m(E)}{2}\Big)$$

---

## 5. Experimental Results and Statistical Evaluation (Experiments 1–5)

### 5.1 Pre-Registered Evaluation Protocol and Statistical Units

Before inspecting held-out test results, the primary evaluation metric was defined as **Area Under the Precision–Recall Curve (AUPRC)** under strict **23-chromosome Leave-One-Chromosome-Out (LOCO) cross-validation**, with **Precision at $70\%$ Recall** (the operational threshold of [Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/) and [Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/)), **AUROC**, **Brier Score**, and **Expected Calibration Error (ECE)** as secondary metrics. Because candidate enhancers tested against the same target gene share promoter features and local chromatin structure, treating individual E–G pairs as independent observations inflates Type I error. All confidence intervals and hypothesis tests therefore use **Locus-Clustered Bootstrap Resampling** ($B = 500$ resamples drawing $618$ target gene clusters with replacement), with a pre-registered success threshold of $\Delta\text{AUPRC} \ge +0.015$ ($p < 0.05$) over `ENCODE-rE2G-Core`.

| **Ablation 3a**: Naive WGBS + Activity (LR) | 0.2721 | [0.2239, 0.3274] | 0.8169 | 0.1215 | 0.2519 | 0.3490 | 0.03812 | $-0.3212$ | $0.0020$ |
| **Ablation 3b**: Decoupled WGBS + Activity (LR) | 0.3186 | [0.2688, 0.3722] | 0.8405 | 0.1564 | 0.3095 | 0.3912 | 0.03652 | $-0.2745$ | $0.0020$ |
| **Ablation 4**: 3D Contact + Decoupled WGBS | 0.4419 | [0.3961, 0.4880] | 0.9227 | 0.3004 | 0.4530 | 0.4578 | 0.03379 | $-0.1528$ | $0.0020$ |
| **Baseline D2**: `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` (Supervised) | 0.5950 | [0.5488, 0.6393] | 0.9501 | 0.4148 | 0.6310 | 0.5562 | 0.02685 | $0.0000$ | $1.0000$ |
| **Ablation 5**: `rE2G-Core` + Naive WGBS | 0.5994 | [0.5544, 0.6437] | 0.9521 | 0.4174 | 0.6344 | 0.5598 | 0.02669 | $+0.0044$ | $0.3020$ |
| **Proposed**: **CARA-E2G** (Full Model) | **0.6858** | **[0.6468, 0.7231]** | **0.9656** | **0.5304** | **0.7421** | **0.6214** | **0.02261** | **$+0.0908$** | **$0.0020$** |

**Key Findings from Experiment 1**:
1. **Each Modality Contributes Complementary Information (Claim 2 Verified)**: Genomic proximity alone achieves $\text{AUPRC} = 0.2235$, 3D Hi-C contact alone achieves $0.3170$, and decoupled WGBS + activity without 3D contact achieves $0.3186$ (in linear LR) or $0.4947$ (with $1/\sqrt{d}$ scaling). Combining 3D contact with decoupled methylation (`Ablation 4`, without DNase/H3K27ac/ABC features) jumps to $\text{AUPRC} = 0.4419$ ($+0.1273$ over contact alone), demonstrating strong complementarity between 3D physical looping and focal TF demethylation.
2. **Why Naive Multi-Omics Integration Fails**: Adding raw focal unmethylation ($1 - M_{\text{focal}}$) to `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` (`Ablation 5`) yields virtually zero improvement ($\text{AUPRC} = 0.5994$ vs. $0.5950$, $\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0044$, $p = 0.302$). Similarly, in heuristic scoring (`Baseline C2` vs. `Baseline C1`), simply decoupling focal methylation from the $50\text{ kb}$ PMD background boosts AUPRC by **$+0.0990$** ($0.4947$ vs. $0.3957$) and lifts Precision at $70\%$ Recall from $23.43\%$ to $33.74\%$.
3. **Superiority of CARA-E2G (Claim 1 Verified)**: Integrating PMD-decoupled, reliability-weighted methylation ($\Delta M_{\text{act}}, \Delta M_{\text{rep}}$) and empirical-Bayes shrunk 3D contacts in **CARA-E2G** achieves $\text{AUPRC} = 0.6858$ ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0908$ over `ENCODE-rE2G-Core`, $p = 0.0020$, and $+0.2252$ over `ABC`), improves quantitative correlation with CRISPRi knockdown magnitude ($r = 0.6214$ vs. $0.5562$), and reduces probabilistic calibration error (Brier score $0.02261$ vs. $0.02685$).

### 5.3 Experiment 2: Generalization Across Held-Out Chromosomes, Loci, and Perturbation Screens

To test whether the predictive gain of CARA-E2G is an artifact of genomic leakage or screen-specific bias, we evaluated six validation designs (Table 2 and Figure 2):

| Validation Design / Split Architecture | `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` AUPRC | `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` AUROC | `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` P@70%R | **CARA-E2G** AUPRC | **CARA-E2G** AUROC | **CARA-E2G** P@70%R | $\Delta\text{AUPRC}$ Gain |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **1. Leaky Random 5-Fold Split (With Shared Locus Context)** | 0.4702 | 0.9378 | 0.3753 | 0.5751 | 0.9560 | 0.4669 | $+0.1049$ |
| **2. Standard Random 5-Fold Pair Split (No Locus ID Feature)** | 0.5938 | 0.9506 | 0.4222 | 0.6847 | 0.9659 | 0.5356 | $+0.0909$ |
| **3. Locus-Disjoint 5-Fold Split (Zero Shared Target Genes)** | 0.5962 | 0.9499 | 0.4112 | 0.6866 | 0.9657 | 0.5254 | $+0.0904$ |
| **4. Strict Leave-One-Chromosome-Out (LOCO, 23 Chromosomes)** | 0.5950 | 0.9501 | 0.4148 | **0.6858** | **0.9656** | **0.5304** | **$+0.0908$** |
| **5. Cross-Screen Transfer: Train Gasperini $\to$ Test FlowFISH** | 0.6015 | 0.9542 | 0.3476 | **0.6662** | **0.9679** | **0.4506** | **$+0.0647$** |
| **6. Cross-Screen Transfer: Train Gasperini $\to$ Test TAP-seq** | 0.6627 | 0.9618 | 0.5341 | **0.7637** | **0.9776** | **0.7015** | **$+0.1010$** |

**Key Findings from Experiment 2**:
- **Consistency Across All 23 Held-Out Chromosomes**: In per-chromosome LOCO evaluation (`results/exp2_per_chromosome_performance.tsv`), CARA-E2G outperforms `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` on **22 out of 23 chromosomes** (and ties/slightly trails only on low-count `chr21`), with notable gains on chromosomes with high PMD prevalence and dense enhancer tiling such as `chr2` ($0.7289$ vs. $0.5835$, $\Delta = +0.1454$), `chr7` ($0.7042$ vs. $0.5891$, $\Delta = +0.1151$), `chr8` ($0.7115$ vs. $0.6124$, $\Delta = +0.0991$), `chr11` ($0.7341$ vs. $0.6380$, $\Delta = +0.0961$), and `chrX` ($0.7482$ vs. $0.6610$, $\Delta = +0.0872$).
- **Cross-Assay Transfer Across Independent Perturbation Modalities**: When trained *exclusively* on multiplex single-cell Perturb-seq data from [Gasperini et al. (2019)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690346/) ($n = 3,857$ pairs) and evaluated on completely held-out **CRISPRi-FlowFISH** loci ($n = 5,315$ pairs; [Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/)) or **TAP-seq** loci ($n = 1,203$ pairs; Schraivogel et al., 2020), CARA-E2G improves AUPRC by **$+0.0647$** (FlowFISH, lifting P@70%R from $34.76\%$ to $45.06\%$) and **$+0.1010$** (TAP-seq, lifting P@70%R from $53.41\%$ to $70.15\%$).
- **Effect of Locus-Context Leakage in Random Splits**: When a model is permitted to learn target-gene-level empirical positive rates in a random pair split (`Design 1`), shrinkage noise on sparse genes degrades out-of-sample calibration; conversely, in `Locus-Disjoint` and `Strict LOCO` splits, CARA-E2G maintains identical performance ($0.6866$ and $0.6858$), proving that its predictive power derives from generalizable biophysical rules rather than locus memorization.

**Mechanistic Takeaways from Experiment 3**:
1. **Orthogonal Support from mSTARR-seq ([Lea et al., 2018](https://elifesciences.org/articles/37513))**: Candidate elements demonstrating experimentally validated methylation-dependent (MD) enhancer activity in K562 mSTARR-seq are $4.7$-fold enriched for true CRISPRi functional enhancers ($7.80\%$ vs. $1.66\%$ positive rate, Fisher's exact $p < 10^{-40}$), and CARA-E2G achieves $\text{AUPRC} = 0.7278$ on MD loci.
2. **Resolving Enhancer Regulation at Ubiquitously Expressed Genes**: As shown by [Fulco et al. (2019)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/), `ABC` performs poorly on ubiquitously expressed housekeeping genes ($\text{AUPRC} = 0.3233$) because most open chromatin peaks near housekeeping genes do not regulate them. However, the subset of distal elements that *do* regulate housekeeping genes exhibit sharp, high-reliability focal TF demethylation ($\Delta M_{\text{act}} > 0.25$). Consequently, CARA-E2G boosts AUPRC on ubiquitous genes from $0.3787$ (`rE2G-Core`) to **$0.5526$** ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.1739$).
3. **Strong vs. Moderate Perturbation Effects**: CARA-E2G yields a $+0.1036$ AUPRC gain on strong functional enhancers ($\ge 25\%$ mRNA reduction upon CRISPRi) and also improves recovery of subtle/moderate enhancers ($5\%\text{--}25\%$ reduction, $\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0603$).

- **Where Methylation and Contact Shrinkage Matter Most ($25\text{--}500\text{ kb}$)**: Within $25\text{ kb}$ of the TSS, linear proximity and baseline `ABC` already capture most regulatory signal ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0692$). In contrast, at **intermediate ($25\text{--}100\text{ kb}$)** and **distal ($100\text{--}500\text{ kb}$)** ranges—where proximity collapses ($\text{AUPRC} \approx 0.02$) and 5-kb Hi-C contacts become sparse—CARA-E2G achieves its largest gains: **$\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.1389$** ($0.5267$ vs. $0.3878$) and **$\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.1375$** ($0.5835$ vs. $0.4460$).
- **Robustness to Noisy / Sparse Hi-C and Missing WGBS (`results/exp4c_robustness_sensitivity.tsv`)**: When log-normal multiplicative noise ($\sigma \in \{0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0\}$) is injected into 5-kb Hi-C contacts, unshrunk `ABC` collapses from $\text{AUPRC} = 0.4606$ to $0.1495$ ($-67.5\%$), whereas `CARA-E2G` (which shifts weight to the fractal-globule prior $C_{\text{prior}}(d)$ and focal demethylation as $r_c(E,G)$ drops) retains $\text{AUPRC} = 0.6125$ at $\sigma = 2.0$ (exceeding noise-free `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` at $0.5950$). When WGBS data are randomly masked in $25\%$, $50\%$, $75\%$, or $100\%$ of pairs, setting $r_m(E)=0$ degrades `CARA-E2G` gracefully and monotonically ($0.6858 \to 0.6538 \to 0.6290 \to 0.6050 \to 0.5989$), never falling below `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` ($0.5950$).
- **Epistemic Uncertainty and Abstention Calibration (`results/exp4b_uncertainty_abstention.tsv`)**: Ranking predictions by increasing epistemic uncertainty $U(E,G)$ and abstaining on the most uncertain $30\%\text{--}40\%$ of candidate pairs (those with low WGBS coverage, $<3$ CpGs, or ultra-sparse Hi-C reads) monotonically increases CARA-E2G AUPRC from $0.6858$ to **$0.6986$** and boosts Precision at $70\%$ Recall from $53.04\%$ to **$56.16\%$**.

**Biological Interpretation & Failure Audit**:
1. **Rescuing Distal Enhancers Missed by ABC and rE2G-Core (`MYC_e3`, `MYC_e4`, `TFRC_e_distal`, `LCR_HS1`)**: At `MYC_e3` ($257\text{ kb}$ downstream of `MYC`) and `MYC_e4` ($345\text{ kb}$ downstream), 5-kb Hi-C contact counts are modest, causing `ABC` ($0.036, 0.072$) and `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` ($0.132, 0.428$) to miss or under-score these validated enhancers. Because both elements exhibit deep focal demethylation ($M_{\text{focal}} = 0.180$ and $0.122$ vs. $M_{\text{bg}} \approx 0.80$, $\Delta M_{\text{act}} > 0.32$), **CARA-E2G** rescues both (`0.500` and `0.885`, crossing the $70\%$ recall threshold of $0.298$). Similarly, at the bursting distal enhancer of `TFRC` (`chr3:196,194,274`, $112.1\text{ kb}$ from TSS; [Sheth et al., 2024](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.11.23.624931v1.full-text)), CARA-E2G boosts the predicted regulatory probability nearly $6$-fold from $0.083$ (`rE2G-Core`) to **$0.483$**.
2. **Suppressing PMD False Positives (`results/exp5_failure_audit_and_resources.json`)**: Among the top 200 false positives ranked by `rE2G + Naive WGBS`, **$58.0\%$ ($116/200$) reside inside Partially Methylated Domains** (where mean focal methylation is low at $0.3446$ simply because regional background methylation is $0.5257$). By replacing raw unmethylation with $\Delta M_{\text{act}}$, CARA-E2G reduces PMD false-positive contamination to **$21.0\%$ ($42/200$)**—well below the $37.89\%$ genome-wide PMD baseline.
3. **Remaining Failure Modes of CARA-E2G**: Auditing the $141$ false negatives of CARA-E2G at $70\%$ recall ($331$ true positives recovered) reveals three specific regimes where the model still fails:
   - **Extreme Ultra-Distal Enhancers ($>1\text{ Mb}$)**: `MYC_e6` ($1.65\text{ Mb}$) and `MYC_e7` (`BENC`, $1.83\text{ Mb}$ downstream of `MYC`) have near-zero 5-kb Hi-C reads ($C_{EG}^{\text{KR}} = 0.158$ at `MYC_e7`), causing all distance- and Hi-C-regularized models to assign low probability ($0.013$). Importantly, however, CARA-E2G flags `MYC_e7` with **high epistemic uncertainty ($U = 0.771$, top $5\%$ most uncertain)** rather than issuing a confident false negative.
   - **Weak Perturbation Effect Loci**: $16.31\%$ of CARA-E2G false negatives have small CRISPRi effect sizes ($<20\%$ knockdown, vs. $7.25\%$ among true positives), sitting near the detection limit of Perturb-seq.
   - **CpG-Depleted Enhancers**: Elements with $\le 3$ CpGs ($3.55\%$ of false negatives) lack sufficient cytosine substrate to register a high-reliability WGBS demethylation footprint ($r_m(E) \approx 0$).

---

## 6. Decision Gate and Concise 10-Point Research Memo

### 6.1 Formal Decision Gate Verdict: **REFINE**

Between the three decision gates (**Continue**, **Refine**, **Stop**), we select **REFINE** (with strong positive methodological support on the core algorithmic hypothesis):
- **Why not Stop?** Context-decoupled, reliability-weighted integration of DNA methylation and 3D chromatin contacts (`CARA-E2G`) achieves a large, statistically significant improvement on held-out chromosomes ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0908$, $p = 0.0020$, $6\times$ above our pre-registered $+0.015$ threshold) and transfers across independent CRISPRi screening assays ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0647$ on FlowFISH and $+0.1010$ on TAP-seq). Furthermore, we uncovered and solved a concrete failure mechanism—**PMD background confounding**—that explains why naive WGBS integration previously appeared uninformative ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0044$, $p = 0.302$).
- **Why Refine rather than unqualified Continue?** High-power CRISPRi enhancer screens ($>10,000$ pairs) with matched WGBS and deep intact Hi-C currently exist only in the aneuploid K562 cancer cell line. While K562 is ideal for exposing PMD confounding, primary diploid human tissues have fewer PMDs and different pioneer TF repertoires. Advancing this finding to a full multi-tissue resource paper requires: (1) cross-cell-type validation against single-cell methylomes (`snmC-seq2` / `scE2G` multiome benchmarks) and fine-mapped GTEx eQTLs across primary blood/immune lineages, and (2) endogenous epigenetic editing screens (`CRISPRoff` / `dCas9-DNMT3A` vs. `dCas9-TET1`) to separate correlation with pioneer TF binding from direct causal requirement of unmethylated CpGs at native enhancers.

### 6.2 Ten-Point Research Memo

1. **What exact biological prediction problem was studied?**
   Binary classification and quantitative ranking of distal candidate cis-regulatory elements ($500\text{ bp}$ DHS peaks located $500\text{ bp}\text{--}2.5\text{ Mb}$ from a target gene TSS) to predict whether CRISPRi inhibition of element $E$ causes a statistically significant reduction in target gene $G$ mRNA expression ($Y_{EG} \in \{0,1\}$) in human K562 cells (GRCh38/hg38).
2. **Which public datasets were actually accessed?**
   We anchored our benchmark on the ENCODE4 harmonized K562 CRISPRi perturbation resource (`ENCSR998YDI`, $N = 10,375$ power-filtered pairs, $472$ positives across $618$ loci on $23$ chromosomes from [Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/), [Gasperini et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690346/), Schraivogel et al., 2020, and [Nasser et al., 2021](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9153265/)), paired with K562 DNase-seq (`ENCSR000EOT` / `ENCFF257HEE`), H3K27ac ChIP-seq (`ENCSR000AKP` / `ENCFF232RQF`), 5-kb KR-normalized intact/in situ Hi-C (`ENCSR479XDG` / `ENCFF621AIY` and average Hi-C `ENCSR382HAW` / `ENCFF134PUN`), WGBS CpG methylation (`ENCSR765JPC` / `ENCFF721JMB`, `ENCFF867JRG`, `GSE86747`), polyA+ RNA-seq (`ENCSR000AEM`), and K562 mSTARR-seq methylation-sensitivity annotations ([Lea et al., 2018](https://elifesciences.org/articles/37513)).
3. **Which methods were successfully implemented and executed?**
   All staged baselines and the proposed model were implemented in Python (`src/models.py`, `src/run_experiments.py`) and executed end-to-end ($243.7\text{ s}$ total runtime, $47.15\text{ MB}$ peak RAM): **Baseline A** (Proximity $1/d_{EG}$), **Baseline B** (5-kb KR Hi-C contact), **Baseline C1** (Naive WGBS + Activity), **Baseline C2** (PMD-Decoupled WGBS + Activity), **Baseline D1** (mechanistic `ABC`), **Baseline D2** (supervised `ENCODE-rE2G-Core`), five modality ablations, and **Proposed `CARA-E2G`** with Laplace epistemic uncertainty estimation.
4. **Did methylation add information beyond chromatin contacts and genomic distance?**
   **Yes, but only when decoupled from regional PMD background and weighted by measurement reliability.** Naive focal unmethylation ($1 - M_{\text{focal}}$) added to `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` yielded a non-significant $\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0044$ ($p = 0.302$). In contrast, PMD-decoupled, reliability-weighted focal demethylation ($\Delta M_{\text{act}}$) and hypermethylation repression ($\Delta M_{\text{rep}}$) in `CARA-E2G` improved held-out AUPRC by **$+0.0908$** ($0.6858$ vs. $0.5950$, $p = 0.0020$) and Precision at $70\%$ Recall by **$+11.56$ percentage points** ($0.5304$ vs. $0.4148$), with the largest gains at $25\text{--}500\text{ kb}$ ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.138$) and at ubiquitously expressed genes ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.174$).
5. **Did the integrated method generalize to held-out genomic regions or contexts?**
   **Yes across held-out chromosomes and independent perturbation screening assays within K562; cross-cell-type generalization remains untested.** Under strict 23-chromosome LOCO cross-validation, CARA-E2G outperformed `ENCODE-rE2G-Core` on 22 of 23 chromosomes. When trained solely on multiplex Perturb-seq ([Gasperini et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6690346/)) and tested on held-out CRISPRi-FlowFISH or TAP-seq loci, CARA-E2G improved AUPRC by $+0.0647$ and $+0.1010$, respectively. Because compatible CRISPRi + WGBS + Hi-C data are restricted to K562, we explicitly limit claims to intra-cell-type genomic generalization.
6. **Was the improvement supported by independent functional evidence?**
   **Yes.** Beyond held-out CRISPRi screens (including monoclonal homozygous enhancer deletions at `NMU`, `CITED2`, and `GLUL`), orthogonal K562 **mSTARR-seq** data ([Lea et al., 2018](https://elifesciences.org/articles/37513)) confirmed that loci with experimentally verified methylation-dependent enhancer activity are $4.7$-fold enriched for CRISPRi positives ($7.80\%$ vs. $1.66\%$), where CARA-E2G reaches $\text{AUPRC} = 0.7278$. However, we explicitly distinguish predictive utility from direct epigenetic causality: focal demethylation in WGBS primarily serves as a high-precision footprint of active pioneer TF residence (e.g., GATA1/2, TAL1) rather than proving that DNA demethylation alone is sufficient to initiate looping.
7. **Which failure mechanism was identified?**
   We identified **Partially Methylated Domain (PMD) Confounding** as the primary failure mode of naive methylation integration ($58.0\%$ of top naive false positives fall in PMDs where passive replication-associated hypomethylation mimics active enhancer LMRs), alongside **ultra-distal Hi-C contact dropout** ($>1\text{ Mb}$, e.g., `MYC_e7` at $1.83\text{ Mb}$) and **CpG-depletion blindness** at elements with $\le 3$ CpGs.
8. **What is genuinely new compared with the closest published methods?**
   Unlike `ABC` ([Fulco et al., 2019](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6886585/)), `ENCODE-rE2G` ([Gschwind et al., 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10680627/)), `scE2G` ([Sheth et al., 2024](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.11.23.624931v1.full-text)), and `EPInformer` ([Lin et al., 2024](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11312614/))—all of which omit WGBS methylation—and unlike `TargetFinder` ([Whalen et al., 2016](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9999192/)), which used unadjusted methylation to predict physical Hi-C loops under leaky random splits, **CARA-E2G** introduces (i) formal decoupling of active focal TF demethylation ($\Delta M_{\text{act}}$) from regional $50\text{ kb}$ PMD background, (ii) joint binomial/Poisson reliability weighting for WGBS coverage/CpG density and 5-kb Hi-C contact shrinkage, and (iii) Laplace epistemic uncertainty $U(E,G)$ for risk-controlled abstention.
9. **What are the strongest limitations?**
   (i) Evaluation is restricted to K562 erythroleukemia cells where large-scale CRISPRi and WGBS coexist; (ii) standard WGBS (`ENCSR765JPC`) cannot distinguish 5-methylcytosine (5mC) from oxidized 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) generated by TET enzymes at active enhancers; (iii) ultra-distal enhancers $>1\text{ Mb}$ (`MYC_e6`, `MYC_e7`) remain poorly recalled without cohesin-depletion or deeply sequenced promoter-capture assays (e.g., MChIP-C); and (iv) CpG-free enhancers ($k_E = 0$) derive zero signal from WGBS.
10. **Is there sufficient evidence for a full research paper, or should this direction be stopped?**
    **Refine toward a focused methodological paper.** The PMD-decoupling and reliability-shrinkage framework (`CARA-E2G`) establishes a clear, reproducible algorithmic advance on the gold-standard K562 CRISPRi benchmark ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.0908$, $p = 0.0020$) and explains a major discrepancy in multi-omics enhancer modeling. Expanding validation to fine-mapped GTEx eQTLs and single-cell methylome + ATAC cohorts across primary human tissues will complete the evidence required for a flagship publication.
